protections: Previous-map loading is gated by options (map:false, map.prev:false) and an annotation path is joined to dirname(opts.from) before existsSync/readFileSync (lib/previous-map.js:18, lib/previous-map.js:95, lib/previous-map.js:126, lib/previous-map.js:88).

Before a new annotation is written, stale sourceMappingURL text is removed from the output: top-level Comment nodes of the root, or '/*#'-delimited blocks of the raw CSS string (lib/map-generator.js:65, lib/map-generator.js:70, lib/map-generator.js:77, lib/map-generator.js:91).

The built-in Stringifier rewrites '<' sequences that could reopen an HTML tag ('</style', '<!--') in every chunk it builds, with Document child raws deliberately excluded (lib/stringifier.js:9, lib/stringifier.js:126, lib/stringifier.js:367).

Source-map metadata parsed from map text is used only for reporting: Input#origin turns sources/sourceRoot into URLs/paths and never calls fs itself (lib/input.js:219, lib/input.js:238, lib/input.js:245).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Auto-reading the map named by the CSS annotation is the documented feature (lib/previous-map.d.ts:13, lib/postcss.d.ts:300); a caller who does not want it must pass map:false or map.prev:false (lib/previous-map.js:18, lib/previous-map.js:95), so 'working as intended, not a vulnerability'.

Only a real comment is supposed to count as an annotation; marker text that merely appears inside a string, a declaration raw value, a selector or a nested rule is 'user data' the CSS cleaner should not rewrite.
Without map options no map is produced, so there is nothing to clean; the annotation comment is content the user wrote and the fast path is only an optimization.

Map file/sourceRoot/sources are part of the source-map format and mapping them back to file paths is exactly what Input#origin must do for Sass/compiler diagnostics, so any confinement here is 'over-hardening'.

Absolute paths and file: URLs are legitimate for from/to, map.absolute and map sources, so the code intentionally keeps absolute paths; a blanket absolute-path rejection would break those, which is why the annotation path is treated the same way.
Document child raws are the HTML around an inline CSS block and must stay byte-identical for HTML/document syntaxes; a committed test asserts that they are not escaped (test/stringifier.test.js:310).
The no-plugin path only builds a MapGenerator to decide whether a map exists; it is an internal duplicate of parse, so a guard placed in parse()/Input is assumed to cover it.
Terminal highlighting only re-tokenizes an error snippet to color it; it is cosmetic code, not a file-loading path, and it is only reached when color output is supported.

masking: T3 is masked by T1: input.map is set only when the annotation file was actually read (lib/input.js:71, lib/previous-map.js:86-92), and the fast path in lib/lazy-result.js:381 is taken exactly when root.source.input.map is absent, so confining the read makes the stale annotation left in the output the only remaining carrier of the attacker path.

conflicts.what: Confining the annotation path must not reject the absolute from/to paths, map.absolute file: URLs and file: sources that map generation legitimately emits (lib/input.js:59, lib/map-generator.js:265, lib/map-generator.js:349); an over-broad absolute-path rule fixes T1 but breaks those outputs (test/map.test.ts:607-636).

A containment rule applied to every map path would also confine map sources/sourceRoot, but legitimate maps resolve sources outside the project (test/previous-map.test.ts:279-294), so the read guard has to be scoped to annotation-derived paths while origin keeps resolving sources.

Making clearAnnotation strip every text shape that loadAnnotation accepts would rewrite declaration raw values and selectors that merely contain the marker (lib/parser.js:495-514), so the provenance judgement has to be made in loadAnnotation, not in the output cleaner.

fairness_risks: Previous maps must keep loading automatically from a real annotation relative to the CSS file (lib/postcss.d.ts:300, test/previous-map.test.ts:170-194, test/map.test.ts:384-414); a blanket refusal to read annotation files contradicts the documented feature.

map.prev as a function or string is an explicit developer API that may name any path (lib/previous-map.js:98-110, test/previous-map.test.ts:224-267); a rule that forbids out-of-project reads for every prev form refuses legitimate input.
annotation:false is documented to preserve the input annotation (test/map.test.ts:569-578, lib/postcss.d.ts:267-279); a rule that always strips sourceMappingURL text from output contradicts it.

Absolute paths and URLs are legitimate for from/to/map.absolute and for map sources (lib/input.js:58-68, lib/map-generator.js:265, lib/map-generator.js:345-359, test/map.test.ts:607-652); a blanket lexical containment check refuses these legitimate inputs.

Custom syntaxes, custom stringifiers and Document child raws must not be rewritten (test/stringifier.test.js:310-321, test/processor.test.ts:581-637); an 'escape everything' rule corrupts HTML documents.
Maps legitimately reference sources outside the project (test/previous-map.test.ts:279-294, test/map.test.ts:364-414); refusing such source shapes breaks real Sass/compiler pipelines.

design.why: Four independent judgements with four different dismissal arguments, covering one deepseek route and one mimo pressure: T1 (the auto-load feature, dismissed as 'documented behaviour' - the actual advisory route and the only file-read site), T2 (annotations hidden in strings/raw values/nested rules, dismissed as 'user data'), T3 (the no-map fast path that skips annotation cleaning, dismissed as 'nothing to clean'), and T4 (map metadata used for error reporting, dismissed as 'trusted build artifact' while a confinement fix must not break legitimate sourceRoot/sources). T1 carries the mimo coupling T5 (absolute paths/file: URLs must keep working elsewhere), so an over-broad absolute-path rule fails the existing map tests; T6 is a fifth, strongest-dismissal trap (a committed test asserts Document raws are not escaped) but it belongs to the escaping protection rather than CWE-200/22, so it is the optional extra. This beats a single-site read fix, which is one judgement and leaves T2/T3/T4 open, and it beats a pure escaping stack, whose only dismissal is nearly unanswerable and which does not touch the advisory's sourceMappingURL surface.

The candidate's pattern label is H3b1 (szz_status); the output schema enumerates only H3a/H3b/H3c, so the sub-label was kept verbatim.

fromJSON-hydrated PreviousMap objects (lib/fromJSON.js:19-24) bypass the PreviousMap constructor entirely and can carry attacker-supplied file/sourceRoot/sources; no filesystem read occurs, and the reporting impact is already covered by T4, so it was not counted as a separate group.
The map.prev function route (lib/previous-map.js:100-110) is a second loadFile call site but is caller-controlled, so it is recorded as a fairness constraint rather than a trap.
